pairs.why: Real cards show visible tone-on-tone concentric rings behind a floating hero; A's rings read slightly more clearly while B's are fainter.
The real locker fills the frame near a wall with baseboard and floor; A matches that framing while B shrinks the locker and adds lots of empty floor.
The real desert is a few large quiet mesas and a thin flat pad with no sun or clouds; both drawings add sun, clouds, shrubs and a thick cracked slab.
Both use wide soft green vertical stripes like the real card, so the backdrops give no reason to choose.
The real card is a striped wall with a clear horizon and a tabletop with a single seam; A keeps that wall-and-ledge staging while B tilts the floor boards and shrinks the wall.
Backdrops are identical; A's plain wooden ledge is quieter and closer to the real ledges, while B's ornate stand and inner swirl add decoration the real cards lack.
The real truss is cropped large at the top edge in a soft beam backdrop; A crops the truss large like that while B shrinks it into a small floating prop.
The real card is a gradient wall with a broad floor curve; A has a wide floor plane with a plain horizon while B turns the floor into a boxy platform with a hard edge.
